text: One morning, he finally came to a senses. He thought about his father's house. Even the people who work for my father have more than enough to eat, he thought. And here I am, starving. He washed his face at a hand pump. He could no longer pretend that everything was fine. I'll go home, he decided. I'll tell my father I've sinned against God and against him. I'm no longer worthy to be called his son anymore. Perhaps he'll let me work for him instead. He set off with very little. Along the way he took odd jobs in the fields. Sometimes a truck gave him a ride. Often he walked barefoot carrying his shoes. At last the familiar fields came into view. Then he saw his father's house.
